chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn 'Isa from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about drinking from a cup that has a silver rim, so he said, 'There is no harm, unless one dislikes silver, in which case he should remove it.'

key_terms.ضَبَّةُ فِضَّةٍ: Silver rim or band on a vessel

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to drink from a cup with a silver rim in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that drinking from vessels with silver rims is legally permissible (ja'iz), distinguishing this ruling from the stricter prohibition often associated with gold. The mention of 'karaha' (dislike) indicates a recommended precaution (istihbab) rather than a mandatory obligation, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of avoiding ostentation while maintaining ritual purity in daily acts.
